title: The Impact of Bank Financing on Borrowers' Voluntary Disclosures and Real Investments
authors: Mingyi Hung; Yupeng Lin; Lynn Linghuan Wang; Zilong Zhang
eligible_reason: Single common shock: Sample_construction_final.do line 41 sets Post = (datadate >= 21 Dec 2011), the first ECB LTRO allotment, for every firm; Treat = 1 for U.S. borrowers of EU banks (time-invariant). In fiscal-year time Post switches on in fyear 2011 only for firms whose FY2011 ends on or after 21 Dec 2011 (125 of 911 fyear-2011 rows are Post = 0) and in fyear 2012 for the rest, so adoption varies only through fiscal-year-end month around one policy date. Following the mnsc.2024.04447 precedent (variation only through fiscal-year-end month = essentially a single policy date), this is not a staggered design. Table 4A col 2 (FREQ_CPX on TreatxPost, firm FE + state-by-year FE, no controls; Regression_final.do line 75) and the no-control columns of Table 5B (Bond1, Equity1) and Table 6B (Investment) would otherwise be clean TWFE columns; most other columns add lagged firm controls ($CONTROLS) or CEM weights.
design_notes: Stata reghdfe. Firm-year panel 2007-2017 (12,417 obs; final_sample_2024_final.dta). Table 3: loan-level reghdfe LOANS/AMT_LOC Treat_bankxPost, absorb(bank_id firm_year) (Khwaja-Mian within-firm design). Table 4A/4B: reghdfe FREQ_CPX TreatxPost [Post] [$CONTROLS], absorb(firm [StateYear]) clu(firm); event study with TP_2010..TP_2015_ (Treat x year) plus controls; CEM-weighted column ([aweight=cem_weights]). Table 5A offshoring splits; Table 5B bond/equity issuance; Table 6 CARs around capex forecasts and investment; Tables 7-8 cross-sectional splits by bank and borrower characteristics.
data_files_note: Analysis datasets shipped (built from Compustat, CRSP, DealScan, I/B/E/S, Thomson, Capital IQ, BankFocus); raw licensed inputs not shipped.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text or PDF). Single LTRO date (Dec 2011); the fyear 2011/2012 split comes only from fiscal-year ends. Flag for the lead if the team wants to revisit the fiscal-year-end rule; the no-control columns (Table 4A col 2; no-control columns of Tables 5B and 6B) would be the candidates.
